paragraphs: This report includes information for multiple registrants, specifically The Williams Companies, Inc. (Williams), as well as Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC (Transco) and Northwest Pipeline LLC (NWP) both of which are wholly owned subsidiaries of Williams (collectively, the Registrants). References to subsidiaries by name, including equity-method investees, Transco, and NWP, refer exclusively to those businesses and operations.

Williams is an energy company committed to being the leader in providing infrastructure that safely delivers natural gas products to reliably fuel the clean energy economy. Williams has operations in 11 supply areas that provide natural gas gathering and processing (G&P), transmission and storage services; NGL fractionation, transportation, and storage services; and marketing services to approximately 800 customers. Williams owns an interest in and operates over 32,000 miles of pipelines in 24 states and in the Gulf of America, 35 natural gas processing facilities, 9 NGL fractionation facilities, approximately 23 million barrels of NGL storage capacity, and 423 Bcf of natural gas storage capacity, and delivers natural gas that is used every day for clean-power generation, heating, and industrial use.

Williams was founded in 1908, originally incorporated under the laws of the state of Nevada in 1949 and reincorporated under the laws of the state of Delaware in 1987. Its common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "WMB." Its operations are located in the United States. Williams' headquarters are located in Tulsa, Oklahoma, with other major offices in Houston, Texas; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; and Salt Lake City, Utah.

Transco owns and operates an approximately 9,600-mile natural gas pipeline system extending from Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and the Gulf of America through Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania and New Jersey to the New York City metropolitan area. The system serves customers in Texas and the 12 southeast and Atlantic seaboard states mentioned above, including major metropolitan areas in Georgia, Washington D.C., Maryland, North Carolina, New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. Transco's principal business is the interstate transportation of natural gas, which is regulated by the FERC.

NWP owns and operates an approximately 3,900-mile natural gas pipeline system, extending from the San Juan basin in northwestern New Mexico and southwestern Colorado through Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, Oregon, and Washington to a point on the Canadian border near Sumas, Washington. The system serves customers in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Wyoming, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, California, and Arizona, either directly or indirectly through interconnections with other pipelines. NWP's principal business is the interstate transportation of natural gas, which is regulated by FERC.
Key variables for Williams' businesses will continue to be:
•Obstacles to Williams' construction and expansion efforts, including delays or denials of necessary permits and opposition to hydrocarbon-based energy development;
•Producer drilling activities impacting natural gas supplies supporting Williams' gathering and processing volumes;
•Retaining and attracting customers by continuing to provide reliable services;
•Revenue growth associated with additional infrastructure either completed or currently under construction;
•Prices impacting Williams' commodity-based activities;
•Disciplined growth in Williams' service areas.

Williams' gathering, treating, and processing operations are presented within the Transmission, Power & Gulf; Northeast G and West reporting segments, as described under the heading "Business Segments."

Williams' gathering systems receive natural gas from producers' crude oil and natural gas wells and gather these volumes to gas processing, treating, or redelivery facilities. Typically, natural gas, in its raw form, is not acceptable for transportation in major interstate natural gas pipelines or for commercial use as a fuel. Williams' treating facilities remove water vapor, carbon dioxide, and other contaminants, and collect condensate. Williams is generally paid a fee based on the volume of natural gas gathered and/or treated, generally measured in the Btu heating value.

General Company Outlook Williams Transco NWP Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Liquidity

Williams is an energy company committed to being the leader in providing infrastructure that safely delivers natural gas products to reliably fuel the clean energy economy. Its operations are located in the United States.

Williams' interstate natural gas pipeline strategy is to create value by maximizing the utilization of its pipeline capacity by providing high-quality, low-cost transportation of natural gas to large and growing markets. Williams' gas pipeline businesses' interstate transmission and storage activities are subject to regulation by the FERC. As such, Williams' rates and charges for the transportation of natural gas in interstate commerce; the extension, expansion, or abandonment of jurisdictional facilities; and accounting, among other things, are subject to regulation. The rates are established primarily through the FERC's ratemaking process, but Williams may also negotiate rates with its customers pursuant to the terms of its tariffs and FERC policy. Changes in commodity prices and volumes transported have limited near-term impact on these revenues because the majority of the cost of service is recovered through firm capacity reservation charges in transportation rates.

The ongoing strategy of Williams' midstream operations is to safely and reliably operate large-scale midstream infrastructure where its assets can be fully utilized and drive low per-unit costs. Williams focuses on consistently attracting new business by providing highly reliable service to its customers. These services include natural gas gathering and processing, treating, compression and storage; NGL fractionation, transportation and storage; and crude oil production handling and transportation, as well as marketing services for NGL, crude oil, and natural gas.

Consistent with the manner in which Williams' CODM evaluates performance and allocates resources, Williams' operations are conducted, managed, and presented within the following reportable segments: Transmission, Power & Gulf; Northeast G West; and Gas & NGL Marketing Services. All remaining business activities, including upstream operations and corporate activities, are included in Other. See Note 1 – Description of Business, Basis of Presentation, and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies for a full description of each segment.

Unless indicated otherwise, the following discussion and analysis of results of operations and financial condition and liquidity relates to Williams' current continuing operations and should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and combined notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data of this report.

In December 2025, Williams paid a regular quarterly dividend of $0.500 per share. On January 27, 2026, Williams' board of directors approved a regular quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share payable on March 30, 2026.
Management's Discussion and Analysis (Continued)

Net income (loss) attributable to The Williams Companies, Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased $393 million compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. Further discussion of the results is found in this report in the Results of Operations.

On August 30, 2024, Transco filed a general rate case with the FERC for an overall increase in rates and to comply with the terms of the settlement of its prior rate case. On September 30, 2024, the FERC issued an order accepting and suspending Transco's general rate filing to be effective March 1, 2025, subject to refund and the outcome of hearing procedures established by the FERC. The order also accepted rate decreases for certain services to be effective as of October 1, 2024. During the third quarter of 2025, Transco reached an agreement in principle with its customers and the other participants to settle all aspects of the rate case and has accrued a related liability for rate refunds. Transco filed with the FERC in October 2025 for approval of the settlement. On December 30, 2025, the FERC approved the settlement which will become effective March 1, 2026.

Williams continues to pursue projects to support the power demands created by new data center and industrial development in power grid-constrained markets, including agreements with a large, investment-grade company to provide onsite natural gas and power generation infrastructure. See Expansion Projects for further discussion.

In December 2025, Williams' management approved a plan to sell certain gas gathering assets in the Mid-Continent region. These operations were designated as held for sale at December 31, 2025 and an impairment, within the West segment, has been recognized for 2025.

In October 2025, Williams entered into an agreement to sell its interests in certain upstream ventures in the South Mansfield area of the Haynesville Shale region, included in Other, for consideration of $398 million with additional contingent consideration to possibly be received through 2029. The transaction closed in January 2026, and Williams expects to recognize a gain in the first quarter of 2026.

paragraphs: 本報告包含多個註冊人之資訊，特別是威廉斯公司（Williams），以及橫跨氣體管線公司（Transco）及西北管線公司（NWP）皆為威廉斯公司百分之百擁有之子公司（合稱為註冊人）。提及子公司名稱之參考，包括權益法投資之子公司、Transco 及 NWP，僅指該等業務與營運。

威廉斯為一家能源公司，致力於成為提供天然氣產品安全基礎設施之領導者，以可靠地供應清潔能源經濟所需。威廉斯在 11 個供應區域進行營運，提供天然氣集輸與處理（G&P）、輸送與儲存服務；NGL 分離、運輸與儲存服務；以及約 800 個客戶之行銷服務。威廉斯擁有並營運逾 32,000 英里之管線，分佈於 24 個州與美洲灣區，35 處天然氣處理設施，9 處 NGL 分離設施，約 2300 萬桶之 NGL 儲存容量，以及 423 億立方英尺之天然氣儲存容量，並提供每日用於清潔發電、供暖與工業用途之天然氣。
威廉斯於 1908 年成立，最初於內華達州法律下於 1949 年設立，並於 1987 年重新於德拉瓦州法律下設立。其普通股於紐約證券交易所交易，代碼為 "WMB"。其營運位於美國。威廉斯總部位於奧克拉荷馬州塔爾薩市，其他主要辦公室位於德克薩斯州休士頓、賓夕法尼亞州匹茲堡及猶他州鹽湖城。

Transco 擁有並營運約 9,600 英里之天然氣管線系統，從德克薩斯州、路易斯安那州、密西西比州與美洲灣區，經由阿拉巴馬州、佐治亞州、南卡羅來納州、北卡羅來納州、弗吉尼亞州、馬裏蘭州、德拉瓦州、賓夕法尼亞州與新澤西州，延伸至紐約市都會區。該系統服務德克薩斯州與上述 12 個東南與大西洋沿岸州的客戶，包括佐治亞州、華盛頓特區、馬裏蘭州、北卡羅來納州、紐約州、新澤西州與賓夕法尼亞州之主要都會區。Transco 的主要業務為天然氣之跨州運輸，並受美國聯邦能源管理局（FERC）監管。

NWP 擁有並營運約 3,900 英里之天然氣管線系統，從美國西北部新墨西哥州桑胡安盆地與西南部科羅拉多州，經由科羅拉多州、猶他州、懷俄明州、愛達荷州、俄勒岡州與華盛頓州，延伸至華盛頓州近 Sumas 地區之加拿大邊界。該系統服務華盛頓州、俄勒岡州、愛達荷州、懷俄明州、內華達州、猶他州、科羅拉多州、新墨西哥州、加利福尼亞州與亞利桑那州之客戶，或透過與其他管線之連接間接服務。NWP 的主要業務為天然氣之跨州運輸，並受美國聯邦能源管理局（FERC）監管。
威廉斯業務之關鍵變數將持續為：
•威廉斯建設與擴張計畫所面臨之障礙，包括必要許可證之延誤或拒絕，以及對基於氫碳化合物能源開發之反對；
•天然氣供應對威廉斯集輸與處理體積之影響，此供應來自於生產者之鑽探活動；
•持續提供可靠服務以留住並吸引客戶；
•因新增基礎建設（已完成或正在施工中）而帶來的收入成長；
•影響Williams商品相關業務的價格變動；
•Williams服務領域的嚴謹成長；
Williams的集氣、處理及處理作業，列為Transmission, Power & Gulf; Northeast G and West應報告分部，如"業務分部"標題所述。
Williams的集氣系統從生產者的原油及天然氣井接收天然氣，並將這些氣體集中至氣體處理、處理及再輸送設施。通常，未處理的天然氣不適合用於主要州際天然氣管線的運輸，也不適合作為燃料商業使用。Williams的處理設施會去除水蒸氣、二氧化碳及其他污染物，並收集凝結物。Williams通常根據集氣及/或處理的天然氣體積（通常以BTU熱值衡量）收取費用。

總體公司展望 Williams Transco NWP 管理層對財務狀況與流動性之討論與分析
Williams 是一家能源公司，致力於成為提供天然氣產品安全輸送基礎設施的領導者，以可靠地為潔淨能源經濟提供燃料。其營運位於美國。

Williams 的跨州天然氣輸氣管線策略是透過最大化其管線容量的使用率，提供高品質、低成本的天然氣運輸服務至大型且持續成長的市場。Williams 的天然氣管線業務之跨州輸送與儲存活動受 FERC 規管。因此，Williams 針對跨州商業運輸天然氣之費用與收費、擴建、擴充或放棄管轄設施、會計等事項，均受規管。費用主要透過 FERC 的費用訂定程序訂定，但 Williams 也可能根據其運費條款與 FERC 政策與客戶協議費用。
Williams 的中游業務持續策略為安全且可靠地運作大型中游基礎設施，使其資產能完全發揮效益，並驅動低單位成本。Williams 聚焦於持續吸引新業務，並為客戶提供高度可靠之服務。這些服務包括天然氣集氣與處理、淨化、壓縮與儲存；NGL 分餾、運輸與儲存；以及原油生產處理及運輸，以及 NGL、原油與天然氣之行銷服務。
Williams 依照其 CODM 評估績效與分配資源的方式，其營運為執行、管理與呈現於以下應報告分部：輸氣、電力與墨西哥灣；東北西；以及天然氣與 NGL 賣方服務。所有剩餘業務活動，包括上游業務與公司活動，均列為其他。詳見附註 1 – 事業說明、財務資料呈現基礎與重要會計政策摘要，以取得各分部之完整說明。
除非另有說明，以下對營運成果與財務狀況及流動性之討論與分析，係針對 Williams 現行持續營運，應配合本報告第二部分，第 8 項財務資料與補充資料所包含之財務報表與合併附註一併閱讀。
2025 年 12 月，Williams 支付了每 share $0.500 的定期季度股息。2026 年 1 月 27 日，Williams 管理委員會批准了每 share $0.525 的定期季度股息，於 2026 年 3 月 30 日支付。
管理層討論與分析（續）

2024 年 8 月 30 日，Transco 向 FERC 提出一般費率案，要求整體提高費率，並符合其先前費率案和解條款之條件。2024 年 9 月 30 日，FERC 發布命令，接受並暫時中止 Transco 之一般費率申請，自 2025 年 3 月 1 日生效，並可請求退款，且須遵循 FERC 所設立之聽證程序結果。該命令亦接受部分服務之費率降低，自 2024 年 10 月 1 日生效。2025 年第三季，Transco 與其客戶及其他參與者達成原則性協議，解決所有費率案之相關事項，並已針對費率退款確認相關負債。Transco 於 2025 年 10 月向 FERC 提交批准該和解之申請。2025 年 12 月 30 日，FERC 批准該和解，將於 2026 年 3 月 1 日生效。
Williams 繼續推動專案，以支持新資料中心及工業發展所產生之電力需求，尤其在電力供應受限市場，包括與一家大型、投資等級公司簽訂協議，提供廠區天然氣與電力發電基礎設施。有關擴張專案之進一步討論請參見擴張專案部分。
2025 年 12 月，Williams 管理層批准出售部分位於中西部地區之天然氣集氣資產之計畫。這些業務於 2025 年 12 月 31 日被指定為待售資產，並於 2025 年內於西區認列減損。
民國114年10月，Williams與他人簽訂協議，出售其在Haynesville Shale地區South Mansfield區域特定上游合作案的權益，包含在其他項目中，交易對價為398 百萬美元，並可能於2029年前收到額外的附條件對價。該交易於民國115年1月完成，Williams預期於2026年第一季認列收益。
